notes:
Lead source: inbound free-credits signup. Small ecommerce platform (merchant integrations, order ops). Primary need: hosted API so they don't manage infra. Current POC goal: build chat assistant that can call internal tool endpoints (update_order, check_inventory) and return structured JSON payloads that can be parsed by their backend. Pain points observed:
- Streaming JSON mode: when using streaming + JSON mode they see partial JSON objects on client side; sometimes final chunk missing closing brace. Customer: 'We get half the object and our parser fails.'
- Function/tool-calling schema mismatch: their frontend validates against a strict schema. When model returns fields in different order or omits optional fields, validation fails. They expect consistent property ordering and explicit nulls for absent optional keys.
- Intermittent function calls: with function_call=auto model sometimes returns text instead of a function call; SE suspects prompt framing and system message differences across sessions.
- Cost sensitivity: concerned about token count for streaming large tool outputs across many concurrent chats; asked about batching and caching guidance.
- Logging/traceability: wants request/response traces for debugging (token-level) but cannot ship full logs containing customer emails. Asked if we can support redacted request logging or pointer to audit log entries.
- Quote from engineering: 'When stream is interrupted, the last chunk lacks trailing metadata so our JSON assembler cannot recover — need either chunk-safe framing or guaranteed finalization.'
Actions so far: provided sample prompt templates (drive link), shared best-practice doc for function schemas, suggested use of validate_schema in client side and post-hoc repair heuristics. SE attempted repro in staging with 3 different model variants; reproduced JSON truncation at ~2% of runs when network drop simulated.
Customer asks: 1) Can Redwood guarantee a finalization token or checksum for streamed JSON? 2) Any recommended server-side schema to be tolerant (e.g., allow missing optional keys)? 3) Guidance for cost estimates for sustained streaming with 500 daily active users.
Tone: pragmatic, engineer-first, wants quick POC to verify fix. Willing to stay hosted if runtime reliability and observability are clear.
